description: NTNU and SINTEF Digital publish Pyintegrity, a Python toolbox for analysing acoustic well-integrity logs. It loads original ultrasonic pulse-echo waveforms and exposes W2/W1, T3, ABCD and L1 processing algorithms through a shared data interface. Coverage includes real and simulated measurements used to estimate casing thickness and the acoustic impedance of material outside a pipe. Public source, installation instructions and a demonstration notebook are free under Apache 2.0. The toolbox can prepare diagnostic observations for condition and degradation simulations, with model-openfoam offering a related physical-modelling context. A caveat is that inferred impedance depends on acquisition geometry and algorithm assumptions; it is not a direct observation of every barrier defect. The documented environment and interfaces were inspected, but installation, field-data processing and numerical accuracy were not tested.
